entry_points.text: Module init registers the MMIO platform driver; exit unregisters it and releases command-line devices.

The PCI driver binds probe, remove, power, SR-IOV and error handlers; legacy wiring installs full config ops; modern wiring picks config ops by capability presence and installs vector, queue and admin-index handlers.

Single MSI-X setup creates the queue and registers its handler except shared, vectorless or slow cases; bulk MSI-X sizes vectors from callbacks with an optional admin queue; INTx shares one interrupt; discovery falls back from dedicated MSI-X to legacy.
Legacy config ops publish byte access, status, reset, queue handling, features, bus naming and affinity, with status reads exposing device state.

exports.text: Legacy admin access offers an availability predicate, paired common/device read and write entries on shared paths with parent resolution first, and a notify query scanning a bounded table to an end marker, returning BAR plus offset or missing.

Notification stores the selector via per-queue storage; bus naming exposes the parent PCI name; capability mapping validates BAR, length, wrap, alignment and range first; notify offsets follow queue selection.
Admin count and index report only when negotiated, failing on zero count; teardown unmaps in reverse order then releases claimed BARs.
Legacy helpers expose host/guest feature registers, status access, and configuration vector assignment verified by read back.

hazards.text: Notify mapping warns and returns null when scaled offsets exceed the mapped length, else returns a direct offset or mapped window.
Zero status is allowed only via reset; finalization aborts above 32 bits; SR-IOV setup rejects unready, featureless or assigned states; reset and vector programming need read-back flushes.

invariants.text: MMIO matches a fixed name with device-tree/ACPI tables and sleep-gated power ops; the selector defaults to modern; without legacy support probe reports missing and removal is empty.

Probe order follows the force flag with missing-device fallback; legacy claims 0x1000-0x103F at the virtio ABI revision preferring 64-bit DMA; modern claims 0x1000-0x107F, splits IDs at 0x1040, and needs common, status and notify capabilities.

MSI-X setup reserves names/masks, adds an optional affinity pre-vector, requests the config handler first and validates routing; one value marks the slow vector; affinity honors callbacks, dedicated vectors and the slow path.

Registers use select-then-access; 64-bit addresses write low then high half; vector writes flush via read back; queue count reads directly; activation programs size, three area addresses, then routing unless disabled.

Build checks pin register offsets; discovery skips bad BARs and claims matching types; legacy features cover low 32 bits only; extended collection merges selected windows; legacy config moves byte-wise from a mode-dependent base.

locks.text: The admin lock with saved interrupts covers insertion, kick and the completion drain cycle via external spin primitives; opcodes need mask bits except two enumeration opcodes; a full queue retries until progress or breakage.
The device lock with saved interrupts guards dispatch traversal, setup linking and deletion, which skips list removal while a queue is in reset; backend teardown runs unlocked.

state_machines.text: Admin execution gates on negotiated support, chains header/data with status/result segments, maps non-OK status to errors, and always frees; init installs the masked list, then clamps and installs object limits with identifier allocation.
The handler samples status once (the read clears it), ignores empty, forwards config changes upward, and claims handled if any source fired; a helper synchronizes legacy and MSI-X handlers.

Legacy creation rejects missing/active queues and high descriptor addresses, then programs page frame, notify and vector with unwind; modern creation exempts the admin queue, activates, maps notify, and destroys on failure.

Legacy teardown disables the vector, flushes via status read, and deactivates with zero address; modern teardown drops vector and notify maps; bulk teardown clears affinity, frees interrupts, deletes queues, then releases all vector state.

Freeze freezes the device then disables PCI; restore enables, masters, then restores; suspend/resume defer to them unless no-reset support skips both; error paths disable around virtio prepare and re-enable around completion, warning on surprises.

Removal keeps a reference, flags surprise absence, disables virtual functions, unregisters, dispatches by mode, then disables PCI and drops the reference; the container lives until release; legacy unmaps BAR0.

structs.text: The transport embeds the generic device with a legacy/modern register union, active-side flag, readable status, two dispatch lists, a per-vector table, and per-queue handle/link/vector records; a helper recovers the container.

Policy offers dedicated, slow-shared, or fully shared vectors; power ops bind six callbacks; the table claims the Red Hat vendor; roles are 0 and 1; config base is 20/24; admin scatter limit is 4; the allowlist merges legacy and device-parts groups; modern-only guards apply.
